_about: The office staff you can hire from the Books page, and Marge's tips. An accountant is paid a wage every night; they find savings on the day's takings (skill, a share of job pay and shop takings). Pay them under what they ask and some of them help themselves: the chance each night is how far under you pay, times their greed. The jar just shows 'sundries' until you audit.

accountants.name: Priya Nand
accountants.pitch: Twelve years at a firm that moved pianos. Tidy, quiet, hates a receipt out of order.
accountants.line_hire: I'll want the receipts in a shoebox by Friday. The actual shoebox is fine.
accountants.line_short: The wage is a little light for the hours, but the work is good.
accountants.line_caught: I'd never. Check again. Please check again.

accountants.name: Len Ocasio
accountants.pitch: Cheap, cheerful, 'between firms'. Did the books for a scrapyard. Nobody says which one.
accountants.line_hire: Cash is fine. Cash is always fine.
accountants.line_short: Bit light, that. Still, we all do what we can.
accountants.line_caught: Sundries, I said. SUNDRIES. Who audits sundries?

accountants.name: Ferdinand Blum
accountants.pitch: Very good. Knows it. Expects a raise every five days and sulks when it doesn't come.
accountants.line_hire: I'll find you money you didn't know you had. We'll discuss my fee again on Friday.
accountants.line_happy: Found another forty in the fuel receipts. You're welcome.
accountants.line_short: I did mention Friday. I did mention it twice.
accountants.line_caught: A rounding error. Several. In my favour, yes, but rounding.

tips: Heavy on the bottom, fragile in padding, and the rest sorts itself.
Buy what's cheap today and sleep on it. Prices move overnight.
The alley is quicker. The alley is bumpier. Pick one.
A plant and a lamp raise the vibe more than a second beanbag.
Goals pay cash and Rep. The clipboard keeps the list.
If a box meows, open it before the drive.
Eighteen kilos on top of a box is the line. Over it, something inside gives.
Fill the truck from the cab wall out and the floor up. The pads only light when they'll take a box.
Three breaks and the owner comes over. Two and they're already counting.
Pay the accountant what they ask. Sundries is not a real expense.
Rent every five days. Keep that much in the jar and the shop never shuts.
A wrapped sofa takes a floor pad and nothing stacks on it. Load it first.
The right room pays three dollars a piece. The toaster does not live in the bathroom.
Serve by hand before the till rings them up and the whole tip is yours.
Honk at someone on the pavement. Five waves a drive, two dollars each.
Back into the bay, don't nose in. The beeps mean it's counting.
Forgive one owner and the next two take a breath before they shove.
The Books page shows where the money went. Read it before you blame the truck.
Stack the carried boxes and the floor clears. Open from the top.
Audit the books the day the jar feels light. It costs thirty. Being robbed costs more.
